summary: Fay Mountain tower in Westborough, MA: state tower from 1911, rebuilt 1915 and 1939, re-cabbed 1970 on an Army radar frame, cab gone by 2001; now private with antennas.

facts.design: Three-legged steel frame; the 1970 state fire tower was built on the former Army radar tower's skeleton
facts.status_note: The steel frame still stands, but the fire cab was removed by 2001 and the summit now carries radio antennas (Patch; NHLR).

access.note: Private property reached by a private right-of-way; NHLR notes no sign and no signed directions. No public access found.

facts.agency: Commonwealth of Massachusetts until 1982; then the city of Westboro; now a private landowner (NHLR)

events.note: First tower, 38 ft with an 8-ft cab, began operating October 11, 1911 (Patch). NHLR gives the same 38-foot height and 8-foot cab.
Earliest staffing mention in the sources read: observer William Halloran at the station, in an October 1912 report.
Lookouts John Giblin and Michael E. Lyons logged 385 fires that season.
A 68-foot tower with a 10-foot cab replaced the 1911 tower. Forest Lookouts quotes 1915 newspapers giving 60 ft planned and 71 ft under construction.
NHLR says the old tower was moved to Chester. Patch says it was dismantled.
Destroyed in the Great New England Hurricane, September 21, 1938. NHLR says a temporary tower followed.
After the Army radar was discontinued, the state built a fire tower on the radar tower's frame. Patch gives 85 ft.
Use discontinued and placed on the state's Standing Inactive List. NHLR says the tower was transferred to the city of Westboro, then to a private owner.
Last fire cab removed by 2001 and set on the ground beside the tower (Patch).

corrections.why: Patch gives 85 ft for the 1970 state tower on the radar frame. No source describes a 60-foot structure on the summit; the only 60-foot figure is a March 1915 plan quoted by Forest Lookouts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Patch say 68 ft. March and May 1915 newspapers quoted by Forest Lookouts say 60 ft planned and 71 ft under construction. We used 68 ft, which the two later sources agree on.
The register and Patch say 38 ft. A March 1915 newspaper quoted by Forest Lookouts calls the old tower 30 ft. We used 38 ft.
The register says it was moved to Chester; Patch says it was dismantled. Not resolved; both are reported in the story.
The register says a platform carries antennas; Patch (2011) describes a communications tower with a small building. Both agree no fire cab remains.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 18.3 m height matches no structure in the sources and is corrected to 25.9 m (85 ft, per Patch). Status kept as standing because the steel frame remains. The register's platform and Patch's communications tower differ in detail; both are recorded. Two Facebook posts by the Massachusetts Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter were seen only as search snippets and are not cited. Ownership and current access were not checked against deed or town records.
